<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? Link the issue: Fixes #123 -->

## Types of changes
<!--- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change; `!` in the title)

## Checklist:
<!--- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
- [ ] The title is a Conventional Commit.
- [ ] My code follows the code style of this project (`make hooks` checks it on commit).
- [ ] I added or updated tests.
- [ ] My change requires documentation updates, and I have updated `docs/` accordingly.
- [ ] Users need more than the title to understand it, so I wrote it under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Done questions ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/adeelahmad/lense/blob/main/AGENTS.md#done-questions))
<!--- Tick each one, or write "n/a" and why. -->
- [ ] Goal: delivers what the user wanted, merged on green CI.
- [ ] Agents: usable through the API, MCP or an assistant tool.
- [ ] Zero setup: no new prerequisite, `.env` edit or manual step.
- [ ] Fewest clicks and keystrokes.
- [ ] Configurable: new settings in the web app with defaults; wizard asks only what is required.
- [ ] Light: default install still runs on a Raspberry Pi with cloud models.
- [ ] Private and secure: data local and encrypted, passkeys, threat model updated.
- [ ] Cost: cheapest path, model calls in the activity ledger, budgets respected.
- [ ] User decides: consequential or new actions wait for the user; defaults unchanged.
- [ ] Upgrades: existing installs upgrade safely (upgrade step for stored-data changes).
- [ ] Honest: sources cited; labelled built, in progress or planned.
- [ ] Tests, docs and generated files updated.
- [ ] Open standards; dependencies keep Lens MIT.
- [ ] Result reported with evidence; "refine later" items written down.
